description: FRTDP (*focused RTDP*) keeps a lower bound `L` and an upper bound `U` on `V*`, the optimal expected cost of each state. It gives each state a *priority* from its gap `U − L` and the priorities of its successors. Trials do not sample: they follow the successor with the highest priority, up to a depth limit that grows when deep updates pay off. The run stops when `U − L ≤ ε` at the start state, and the policy is greedy on `U`. Use it like BRTDP when the probable outcomes matter most; the crate adds a BRTDP trial after a trial that does not shrink the gap.

papers.title: Focused Real-Time Dynamic Programming for MDPs: Squeezing More Out of a Heuristic
